subject: Re: Payment cadence & PO flow for Dedicated GPU pool (options + next steps)
messages:
From: Jordan Miles <jordan.miles@acme-analytics.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@acme-analytics.com>
Date: Sat, 14 Feb 2026 09:17:00 -0800
Subject: Payment cadence & PO flow for Dedicated GPU pool

Diego,

Thanks for the productive demo yesterday — Acme is excited about the throughput numbers you showed. Before we proceed with a purchase order, procurement needs clarity on a few billing items so we can align with finance:

1) Invoice cadence: two options on the table from our side — monthly invoices vs. annual prepay w/discount. Finance prefers monthly for cash flow reasons but will accept annual prepay with a clearer True-Up process.
2) True-ups: how you handle overages mid-quarter and whether those get netted on the next invoice or billed immediately.
3) PO flow and SOW: They want to attach a PO to an SOW and confirm acceptance criteria for throughput guarantees (p95 latencies / tokens per second).
4) Net terms: standard 30 vs. 60 days — what can Redwood support for an enterprise account?

Can you share a concise options matrix we can circulate internally (procurement + engineering)? Also please include any impact to discount tiers depending on commit length / prepay.

Appreciate it — copying Priya (finance) to keep the thread visible.

—Jordan
Procurement Manager
Acme Analytics
[Attachment: RFP-Requirements-ACME.pdf (pdf, 90KB)]

From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Miles <jordan.miles@acme-analytics.com>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@acme-analytics.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Feb 2026 11:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Payment cadence & PO flow for Dedicated GPU pool

Jordan — thanks for the clear list. Put together a short matrix below and attached a preliminary quote and SOW draft. High-level options (focused on Dedicated GPU pool / reserved commit):

Option A — Monthly invoicing (no prepay):
- Commitment: 12-month reserved capacity with monthly invoices based on committed baseline.
- True-up: Monthly true-up for consumption above committed baseline; overages billed on the next monthly invoice.
- Discount: baseline price (no prepay discount).
- Net terms: Net 30 standard; Net 60 available with credit review and purchase order integration.
- Pros/Cons: Flexible cash flow for customer; higher unit price vs prepay.

Option B — Annual prepay (one-time prepay at contract start):
- Commitment: 12-month or 24-month prepay for committed GPU pool (preferred for large pools).
- True-up: Quarterly true-up reconcile; minor overages applied to next quarter or (optionally) refunded as credit.
- Discount: 8–16% depending on size and term (higher discount for larger commits and longer terms).
- Net terms: Prepay reduces credit requirements; invoices for true-ups on a 30-day schedule post-reconciliation.
- Pros/Cons: Best unit economics for high-throughput workloads; requires upfront cash.

Option C — Hybrid (monthly billing with capped prepay):
- Commitment: Small upfront commitment (e.g., one month prepay) + monthly baseline.
- True-up: As in Option A but with lower overage rate due to small prepay buffer.
- Discount: modest 3–6% on baseline.

Other notes:
- Throughput guarantees: We provide throughput SLAs at the reserved pool level (tokens/sec and p95 latency targets). Acceptance criteria are defined in the SOW; we recommend a 14-day ramp/test window post-activation.
- PO flow: Redwood accepts POs tied to the SOW. For annual prepay we can accept a PO and invoice per milestone (e.g., 50% on signing, 50% on activation) if that's helpful for Acme cash cycle.

Attached: Redwood_Dedicated_Quote_20260220.pdf (draft pricing grid), SOW_Acme_Redwood_draft_20260220.docx (SOW skeleton including ramp/test criteria).

Next step: Can you confirm which option Procurement prefers and whether Acme needs a milestone invoice schedule for the prepay? If you want, I can loop in our finance lead (Marissa) and legal (Lauren) to finalize PO/SOW terms.

Best,
Diego Fernandez
Enterprise Sales Lead | Redwood Inference
D: +1 415 555 0199
[Attachment: Redwood_Dedicated_Quote_20260220.pdf (pdf, 120KB)]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 17 Feb 2026 09:25:00 -0800
Subject: FW: Payment cadence & PO flow for Dedicated GPU pool

Diego / Rishi — quick internal note on the quote structure before we send a formal redline:

1) Discounting: For Acme-sized pools we can stretch to 12% on annual prepay (24-month) if they commit to a 20% headroom buffer. If they want 12-month prepay only, cap at 8%. Hybrid options can be 4–6% depending on baseline.
2) True-up behavior: prefer quarterly reconciliation for annual prepay (simpler bookkeeping). For monthly billing, overages billed next month is fine; ensure we document the cap rate for emergency burst to avoid surprise bills.
3) PO / Milestone invoicing: Finance prefers not to split annual prepayments into too many milestones (creates revenue recognition overhead). Two milestones (50/50) is acceptable — ensure SOW has clear activation date and acceptance test.
4) Net terms: Net 30 is default. We can offer Net 45 for strategic deals but Net 60 should go through credit ops (we can support if procurement provides a PO and some reference credit docs).

I'll clean up the quote language and add explicit billing schedule examples (sample invoices and a sample PO text). Diego — suggest you propose Option B with quarterly true-up and 50/50 milestone billing as an initial concession, then we can negotiate down to Option A if they insist on monthly cashflow.

—Marissa
Head of Revenue Operations | Redwood Inference

From: Priya Shah <priya.shah@acme-analytics.com>

Cc: Jordan Miles <jordan.miles@acme-analytics.com>
Date: Thu, 19 Feb 2026 10:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Payment cadence & PO flow for Dedicated GPU pool

Diego,

Thanks — that matrix helps. After a quick check with finance, our preference is: Option B (Annual prepay) if Redwood can accept a 50/50 milestone invoice schedule and a quarterly true-up with credits applied to the following quarter. The key asks from our side: 1) p95 latency acceptance tests captured in SOW, 2) a 14-day ramp window, 3) Net 60 on the milestone invoices (this is our standard for large prepayments).

Two quick clarifications: if quarterly true-up shows usage materially above committed baseline (more than 25% over), will Redwood allow an immediate supplemental invoice instead of waiting for next quarter? Finance wants a path for predictable cash flow if usage spikes. Also, can you confirm the discount for a 12-month prepay at our expected size (we're anticipating a 60-GPU pool equivalent)?

We can sign a PO once we have the SOW + milestone invoice language updated.

—Priya
Head of Finance | Acme Analytics

From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Payment cadence & PO flow for Dedicated GPU pool

Priya / Jordan — great, thanks for confirming the preferred path. To be explicit on the items you asked about: 

- Discount for 12-month prepay at ~60-GPU equivalent: 10% (we can move to 12% for a 24-month commit or a 20% buffer guarantee).
- Quarterly true-up: credits applied to following quarter by default. However, for material spikes >25% quarter-over-quarter we will offer an interim supplemental invoice (same rate as overage) to maintain predictability; this is captured in the SOW section 3.2 (billing and true-ups).
- Milestone invoicing: 50% on signed PO, 50% on activation (activation = successful completion of 14-day ramp/test and SOW acceptance criteria). We will invoice milestones and extend Net 60 on the milestone invoices for Acme (credit review complete).
- Throughput acceptance: p95 latency and tokens/sec thresholds will be listed in SOW; 14-day ramp window for tests and a joint sign-off.

Action items:
1) Diego to send revised SOW and final quote with milestone language (attached).
2) Acme to issue PO referencing deal ACME-DED-2026-0034 once SOW reviewed.
3) Redwood finance (Marissa) and legal (Lauren) to finalize the milestone invoice language and credit docs.

Attaching revised quote and SOW draft. Please let me know if you need a payment schedule example for your CFO.

Best,
Diego Fernandez
Enterprise Sales Lead | Redwood Inference
